_comment: Retrieval eval queries. Authored by Claude in the style of real diagnosis root_cause text (see diagnoses_captured.json). expected_entry_ids empty => no runbook entry should match (must route to human authoring). 'dev' queries may be used to tune threshold/margin; 'test' queries are held out and only reported. Caveat: same author as the corpus, so results are optimistic -- add your own queries in retrieval_queries_user.json.

queries.root_cause: The issuer declined a $35.00 charge for insufficient funds. The customer is a standard-tier account with no secondary payment method saved, and this is the first failure with no earlier remediation attempts.
Card declined: available balance too low for the $62.50 charge. Standard tier, no backup card on file, no prior remediation.

The charge of $120.00 was declined as insufficient funds on the primary card. The customer, a standard-tier account, has a second payment method saved on their profile, and no remediation has been tried yet.

decline_code insufficient_funds on a $88.00 USD charge; the cardholder lacks the balance right now. customer_data shows has_backup_payment_method: True and tier standard; case_history shows no prior remediation.
The card on file passed its expiry date, so the gateway rejected the charge; this is a permanent failure of the instrument. The customer does have an alternate payment method on file.
Gateway decline_code 'expired_card' for a $45.00 charge -- the card is past expiration and cannot be charged again. customer_data.has_backup_payment_method is True.
The customer's card has expired and the charge was refused as a permanent instrument failure. There is no other payment method on the account to fall back to.
expired_card decline on a $150.00 charge; the card can never succeed again as-is. has_backup_payment_method: False, standard tier, first failure.

The processor hit an internal error while handling the authorization request. This looks like a temporary fault on the issuer or processor side rather than anything wrong with the card or the account balance.
decline_code processing_error: transient issuer/processor glitch during authorization; card and funds not implicated.
The gateway asked the client to try again later, which points to temporary throttling on the processor side. The instrument and the account are fine.
try_again_later response: the processor is rate-limiting requests temporarily; no issue with the card.
The issuer reported this card as lost or stolen and blocked the charge. This is a fraud-related hard decline on the instrument itself; the customer having a saved backup card does not change that.

queries.note: fraud, standard tier + backup -- must never match
queries.root_cause: The fraud-detection system flagged the transaction as suspected fraud and the issuer refused it. The account is standard tier and has a backup payment method on file, but a fraud flag makes the instrument unusable regardless.
decline_code stolen_card: issuer flagged the payment instrument as stolen. Fraud hold; do not retry.

queries.note: high-value tier funds decline -- tier-sensitive, should not auto-match
queries.root_cause: The charge of $410.00 was declined for insufficient funds. The customer is a high-value tier account with no backup payment method on file and no earlier remediation attempts.

queries.note: high-value tier funds decline, evidence-key style
queries.root_cause: decline_code insufficient_funds, $300.00 USD. customer_data.customer_tier is high_value, has_backup_payment_method False, first failure. The balance is short right now.

queries.note: uncovered failure type: generic issuer refusal
queries.root_cause: The issuer refused the charge with a generic do-not-honor response and gave no reason. This is a permanent decline from the issuer, not tied to expiry, funds or a fraud flag we can see.
The card does not support the currency of this charge, so the gateway rejected it permanently. Not an expiry or fraud issue.

queries.note: uncovered failure type: 3DS required (soft decline that a blind retry cannot fix)
queries.root_cause: The issuer requires customer authentication (3D Secure) before it will approve this charge. Retrying the same request without the customer completing authentication will fail again.

queries.note: uncovered situation: repeated funds failure after prior retry
queries.root_cause: Insufficient funds decline again: a retry was already attempted 24 hours ago for this case and failed with the same code. Standard tier, no backup payment method on file.
